ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $AD=BD$, $F$ is the intersection of the height $AD$ and $BE$, $CD=2$, $AF=3$. What is the length of segment $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $AD$ and $BE$ are the altitudes of the triangle,\\
it follows that $\angle C+\angle DBF=90^\circ$, $\angle C+\angle CAD=90^\circ$, $AD\perp BC$,\\
which means that $\angle DBF=\angle DAC$, $\angle ADB=\angle ADC=90^\circ$,\\
Considering triangles $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle BFD$,\\
we have $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DBF=\angle DAC\\
AD=BD\\
\angle BDF=\angle ADC=90^\circ
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore, $\triangle ACD\cong \triangle BFD$ (by ASA),\\
which implies that $CD=FD$,\\
Given that $CD=2$, $AF=3$,\\
it follows that $BD=AD=FD+AF=2+3=5$,\\
thus $BC=5+2=\boxed{7}$.

which means that $\angle DBF=\angle DAC$, $\angle ADB=\angle ADC=90^\circ$.
Considering triangles $\triangle ACD$ and $\triangle BFD$,

$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DBF=\angle DAC\\
AD=BD\\
\angle BDF=\angle ADC=90^\circ
\end{array}\right.$,
therefore, $\triangle ACD\cong \triangle BFD$ (by ASA),
which implies that $CD=FD$.
Given that $CD=2$, $AF=3$,
it follows that $BD=AD=FD+AF=2+3=5$,
thus $BC=5+2=\boxed{7}$.
